## *** NO qf_models ***
### - JUN protein group

```{r}
jun_accession <- "P05412"

jun_candidates <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(names(qf_models), function(software) {

    rd <- as.data.frame(
      SummarizedExperiment::rowData(
        qf_models[[software]][["proteins"]]
      )
    )

    # Match JUN accession as a complete identifier,
    # including within semicolon-separated protein groups
    hit <- grepl(
      paste0("(^|[;|])", jun_accession, "($|[;|])"),
      as.character(rd$Protein.Group)
    )

    # Also search Protein.Ids where available
    if ("Protein.Ids" %in% names(rd)) {
      hit <- hit | grepl(
        paste0("(^|[;|])", jun_accession, "($|[;|])"),
        as.character(rd$Protein.Ids)
      )
    }

    hit[is.na(hit)] <- FALSE

    data.frame(
      Software = software,
      Protein.Group = as.character(rd$Protein.Group[hit])
    )
  })
)

print(jun_candidates, row.names = FALSE)
```
### - p_jun

```{r}
# Keep candidate groups present in the protein assays
jun_groups <- jun_candidates

# Require one unambiguous JUN protein group per pipeline
stopifnot(
  nrow(jun_groups) == 4,
  all(table(jun_groups$Software) == 1)
)

jun_data <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(names(qf_models), function(software) {

    se <- qf_models[[software]][["proteins"]]

    protein_id <- jun_groups$Protein.Group[
      jun_groups$Software == software
    ]

    data.frame(
      Software = software,
      Run = colnames(se),
      Log2_Intensity = as.numeric(
        SummarizedExperiment::assay(se)[protein_id, ]
      )
    )
  })
) |>
  left_join(sample_design, by = "Run") |>
  mutate(
    Genotype = case_when(
      grepl("^CTRL_", Condition) ~ "CTRL",
      grepl("^KO_", Condition) ~ "KO",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    Genotype = factor(Genotype, levels = c("CTRL", "KO")),
    Software = factor(Software, levels = names(qf_models))
  ) |>
  filter(
    !is.na(Genotype),
    grepl("Untreated|Baseline", Condition, ignore.case = TRUE)
  )

# Check sample coverage before plotting
jun_data |>
  group_by(Software, Batch, Genotype) |>
  summarise(
    Total = n(),
    Quantified = sum(is.finite(Log2_Intensity)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  print(n = Inf)

p_jun <- ggplot(
  jun_data,
  aes(
    x = Genotype,
    y = Log2_Intensity,
    color = Genotype
  )
) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.5,
    outlier.shape = NA,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  geom_jitter(
    width = 0.12,
    size = 2,
    alpha = 0.8,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  facet_grid(Software ~ Batch, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(CTRL = "#0072B2", KO = "#D55E00")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "JUN abundance across DIA pipelines",
    subtitle = "Untreated samples stratified by genotype and acquisition batch",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Normalized log2 JUN protein intensity"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )

print(p_jun)
```
### - p_jun_precursors

```{r}

jun_precursor_data <- bind_rows(
  lapply(names(qf_models), function(software) {

    se <- qf_models[[software]][["precursors_norm"]]
    rd <- as.data.frame(SummarizedExperiment::rowData(se))

    hit <- as.character(rd$Protein.Group) == "P05412"
    hit[is.na(hit)] <- FALSE

    if (!any(hit)) {
      warning("No JUN precursors found in ", software)
      return(NULL)
    }

    x <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(se)[hit, , drop = FALSE]

    data.frame(
      Software = software,
      Precursor = as.character(rd$Precursor.Id[hit])[
        row(x)
      ],
      Run = colnames(x)[col(x)],
      Log2_Intensity = as.vector(x)
    )
  })
) |>
  left_join(sample_design, by = "Run") |>
  mutate(
    Genotype = case_when(
      grepl("^CTRL_", Condition) ~ "CTRL",
      grepl("^KO_", Condition) ~ "KO",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    Genotype = factor(Genotype, levels = c("CTRL", "KO")),
    Software = factor(Software, levels = names(qf_models))
  ) |>
  filter(
    !is.na(Genotype),
    grepl("Untreated|Baseline", Condition, ignore.case = TRUE)
  )

# Check how many JUN precursors each pipeline quantifies
jun_precursor_data |>
  group_by(Software) |>
  summarise(
    Precursors = n_distinct(Precursor),
    Quantified_measurements = sum(is.finite(Log2_Intensity)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  print(n = Inf)

p_jun_precursors <- ggplot(
  jun_precursor_data |>
    filter(is.finite(Log2_Intensity)),
  aes(
    x = Genotype,

) +

    values = c(CTRL = "#0072B2", KO = "#D55E00")

    title = "JUN precursor abundance across DIA pipelines",
```

# -
```{r qc_protein_specific_estimability, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# Protein-specific design rank and contrast estimability
# ============================================================

qf_list <- list(
  AlphaDIA = qf_alpha,
  `DIA-NN` = qf_diann,
  Spectronaut = qf_spectro,
  MaxDIA = qf_maxdia
)

# Reconstruct contrast vectors from the existing design matrix
contrast_matrix <- t(vapply(
  seq_len(nrow(planned_contrasts)),
  function(i) {
    reference_matrix[planned_contrasts$Numerator[i], ] -
      reference_matrix[planned_contrasts$Denominator[i], ]
  },
  numeric(ncol(design_matrix))
))

rownames(contrast_matrix) <- planned_contrasts$Contrast

# Verify that contrast coefficients match the design matrix
stopifnot(
  identical(
    colnames(contrast_matrix),
    colnames(design_matrix)
  ),
  nrow(design_matrix) == nrow(design_data)
)

# Assign actual run names to the design matrix
rownames(design_matrix) <- as.character(design_data$Run)

# Confirm alignment
stopifnot(
  identical(
    rownames(design_matrix),
    as.character(design_data$Run)
  )
)

# Function to evaluate a single observed-sample pattern
check_pattern <- function(observed, X, C) {

  X_obs <- X[observed, , drop = FALSE]

  if (nrow(X_obs) == 0L) {
    return(c(
      Rank = 0,
      Full_Rank = 0,
      setNames(
        rep(0, nrow(C)),
        paste0("Contrast_", seq_len(nrow(C)))
      )
    ))
  }

  # QR rank of the observed design
  rank_obs <- qr(X_obs)$rank

  # SVD-based row-space test for contrast estimability
  sv <- svd(X_obs, nu = 0, nv = ncol(X_obs))

  tolerance <- max(dim(X_obs)) *
    max(sv$d) *
    .Machine$double.eps

  rank_svd <- sum(sv$d > tolerance)

  if (rank_svd == ncol(X_obs)) {

    estimable <- rep(TRUE, nrow(C))

  } else {

    null_basis <- sv$v[
      ,
      seq.int(rank_svd + 1L, ncol(X_obs)),
      drop = FALSE
    ]

    null_projection <- C %*% null_basis

    estimable <- apply(
      abs(null_projection),
      1,
      max
    ) < 1e-8
  }

  c(
    Rank = rank_obs,
    Full_Rank = as.integer(rank_obs == ncol(X)),
    setNames(
      as.integer(estimable),
      paste0("Contrast_", seq_len(nrow(C)))
    )
  )
}

protein_rank_results <- list()
protein_contrast_results <- list()

for (software in names(qf_models_68)) {

  cat("Checking:", software, "\n")

  se <- qf_models_68[[software]][["proteins"]]
  x <- assay(se)

  # Align design matrix to the assay columns
  sample_idx <- match(colnames(x), design_data$Run)

  stopifnot(
    !anyNA(sample_idx),
    !anyDuplicated(sample_idx)
  )

  X <- design_matrix[sample_idx, , drop = FALSE]

  # Finite protein measurements
  detected <- is.finite(x)

  # Group proteins with identical observed-sample patterns
  pattern_key <- apply(
    detected,
    1,
    function(z) paste0(as.integer(z), collapse = "")
  )

  unique_keys <- unique(pattern_key)

  pattern_results <- lapply(unique_keys, function(key) {

    observed <- which(
      strsplit(key, "", fixed = TRUE)[[1]] == "1"
    )

    check_pattern(
      observed = observed,
      X = X,
      C = contrast_matrix
    )
  })

  pattern_results <- do.call(
    rbind,
    pattern_results
  )

  # Map pattern results back to individual proteins
  protein_results <- pattern_results[
    match(pattern_key, unique_keys),
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  protein_rank_results[[software]] <- data.frame(
    Software = software,
    Total_Proteins = nrow(x),
    Unique_Missingness_Patterns = length(unique_keys),
    Full_Rank_Proteins = sum(
      protein_results[, "Full_Rank"] == 1
    ),
    Full_Rank_Percent = 100 * mean(
      protein_results[, "Full_Rank"] == 1
    ),
    Median_Protein_Rank = median(
      protein_results[, "Rank"]
    ),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  protein_contrast_results[[software]] <- data.frame(
    Software = software,
    Contrast = planned_contrasts$Contrast,
    Estimable_Proteins = colSums(
      protein_results[
        ,
        paste0("Contrast_", seq_len(nrow(contrast_matrix))),
        drop = FALSE
      ]
    ),
    Total_Proteins = nrow(x),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

protein_rank_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  protein_rank_results
)

protein_contrast_estimability <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  protein_contrast_results
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Estimable_Percent =
      100 * Estimable_Proteins / Total_Proteins
  )

cat("\nProtein-specific design rank:\n")
print(protein_rank_summary, row.names = FALSE)

cat("\nProtein-specific contrast estimability:\n")
print(
  protein_contrast_estimability,
  row.names = FALSE
)
```
The median protein-specific design rank is 12 for every software pipeline, matching the number of model coefficients. This means that nearly all proteins have sufficient observations across the experimental conditions and acquisition batches to estimate every coefficient in the proposed model. Importantly, the remaining rank-deficient proteins are not necessarily unusable. Some can still support particular biological contrasts.
Protein-specific design matrix diagnostics demonstrated high model identifiability across all four DIA analysis pipelines. Full-rank design matrices were obtained for 98.04% of AlphaDIA proteins, 97.70% of DIA-NN proteins, 99.99% of Spectronaut proteins, and 99.93% of MaxDIA proteins. Across the eleven planned biological contrasts, mathematical estimability exceeded 98.9% for every pipeline. These findings indicate that protein-level missingness is unlikely to substantially restrict differential abundance analysis. Nevertheless, direct comparisons between 6-hour and 24-hour cisplatin treatments remain dependent on additive batch-effect assumptions because the treatment groups were acquired in separate batches. Therefore, subsequent statistical modeling will incorporate acquisition batch as a fixed effect, with cross-time-point comparisons interpreted cautiously.
